solution.title: Deploy a Third-Party PFX Certificate to Mobile Devices for App Use with Microsoft Intune

products.name: Deploy a Third-Party PFX Certificate to Mobile Devices for App Use with Microsoft Intune — Commercial
products.short_description: The correct, repeatable enterprise method to deliver a third-party PFX certificate to iOS/mobile devices via Intune for app use — imported-PFX (Certificate Connector + Graph import) vs custom PKCS12 profile, with a decision guide and the keychain nuance that determines whether the app can use it. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Get a third-party PFX certificate onto iOS devices through Intune — the right way, so the app can actually use it

A third-party PFX certificate — one that behaves like a software/license credential an app consumes, not a standard TLS/SSL cert — needs to land on iOS/mobile devices through Microsoft Intune so a specific app can use it. The usual trap: teams reach for the SCEP or PKCS (CA-issued) template, the request never shows up the way they expect, and the deployment stalls even though the PFX object already exists in Intune/Graph. The reason is simple once you see it: a static, externally-issued PFX is a different delivery path. This solution gives you the correct, repeatable enterprise method to import that PFX and deliver it to devices so the app can consume it.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — how certificate delivery works in Intune and why a static third-party PFX is NOT a SCEP/PKCS (CA-issued) scenario; the two correct paths — a PKCS imported certificate profile (with the Intune Certificate Connector + a Graph PFX import) and a custom iOS configuration profile carrying a PKCS12 payload — and a clear decision guide for the app use case (keychain access).
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, Entra ID, the Intune Certificate Connector and its health, the third-party PFX file + password, the trusted root/intermediate chain, iOS enrollment, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide (the resolution) — exact, ordered steps: confirm the imported PFX object, install/validate the Certificate Connector, import the PFX via Microsoft Graph, deploy the trusted-root chain, create and assign the PKCS imported certificate profile (and the custom PKCS12 profile alternative), then validate the app can use the certificate, pilot, and expand.
  • App-use & keychain guidance — how the certificate is placed on iOS and what determines whether the target app can access the identity (keychain access group / app configuration), with the decision criteria for imported-PFX vs custom-profile delivery; app-internal specifics are deferred to the app vendor.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — certificate-readiness discovery (imported PFX objects + Connector + profiles), per-device certificate-presence validation, a fleet certificate-deployment report, safe remediation (re-assign/repair), and a Graph PFX-import helper that uploads a third-party PFX to Intune.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

A third-party PFX certificate correctly imported into Intune and delivered to iOS devices through the right profile type — with the app able to consume it — instead of stalling on the wrong SCEP/PKCS template, proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • PFXMOB-Discovery.ps1 — inventory imported PFX objects, Certificate Connector status, and
    • PFXMOB-Import-Pfx.ps1 — import a third-party PFX into Intune via Microsoft Graph for a target user
    • PFXMOB-Remediation.ps1 — safely re-assign/repair the certificate delivery profile and re-trigger
    • PFXMOB-Report.ps1 — fleet-wide certificate-deployment status for the iOS app-certificate profiles
    • PFXMOB-Validation.ps1 — per-device check that the trusted chain + identity are present and the

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
